chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Muhammad ibn Sahl, from his father who said:

I asked Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) about the man who rents the house and the ship from the man for a year, or more or less. He (peace be upon him) said: 'Its rent is necessitated up to the time which he had hired it to, and the choice regarding taking the rent is up to its owner, if he so desires to he takes, and if he so desires to he leaves'.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules regarding the duration and termination of a rental contract in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Recorded in *Al-Kafi* by Shaykh al-Kulayni, this hadith from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies the stability of the *ijarah* (rental) contract, establishing that the lessee is bound for the agreed term while the lessor retains the unilateral right of option (*khayr*) to terminate or continue the lease. This ruling underscores the flexibility in Shia commercial jurisprudence, allowing property owners to reclaim their assets or adjust terms even after the contract is initiated, provided the initial duration is respected. It reflects the practical application of contract law in early Islamic society, addressing common assets like dwellings and maritime vessels.
